review_text_raw: I got this game because I really loved Orwell and found it to be a thought provoking and thrilling story experience. This game, although comparable in premise, is definitely unique in its gameplay and purpose--you get prompted to "participate" (I say this loosely because your dialogue options are limited) in text/phone conversations as well as chats with your coworkers, and you can do "off the record" work from home. Like Papers, Please, more surveillance options open up as you play and there is an underlying plot. But I do have some issues with the mechanics of the game; as I mentioned before, dialogue options are very limited, and you're required to pursue certain paths in the story (you can't chose *not* to work for specific groups. You have to take all opportunities or you get a game over, which is kind of annoying). There's also some bugs and small annoying "Features"... The instructions/tutorials/exposition text all automatically progress (no "click to continue") so you can easily miss out on instructions or text. Sometimes the tutorial messages will get stuck and stop proceeding even though you've done what they've asked. Then it won't continue until you've gone ahead and figured out the tutorial section on your own. The game could use some more polish, but isn't unplayable and is fun enough.

review_text_raw:
There's a very good game here, somewhat hidden under a clunky UI. Once you get past some of the unclear instructions, the gameplay is straightforward and can be very enjoyable. You just have to work out the logic behind some of the decisions you're required to make, and that can take one or two do-overs.

I've waited for this game for two years, as have many other people, and I'm choosing to give the devs the benefit of the doubt. Clearly this game is a labour of love and with some tweaks could become a whole lot of fun.

UPDATE 1.02: Just as an addition, the post-launch work that the devs have put in shows that they *are* listening to the community. They are not just fixing bugs but also taking the advice of players to make improvements to gameplay and the UI. This is really good to see.

When I noticed there was a patch and saw that they were listening to the community telling them that the gameplay was confusing and there wasn't enough guidance (which is precisely why I wasn't impressed with the game as well) I got pretty excited.

Downloaded the update, and the new system clarified SO many things I didn't understand, and NOW I have a game to get engrossed in on my Saturday night!

Developers:  WELL DONE!  And if you're still listening, not being able to skip the AI interactions for a new character is a poor design decision.  Please give us a fast forward/skip option!

review_text_raw:
I backed this on Kickstarter, I played the demo and the Kickstarter beta. Both of which were nice examples of the software that worked fairly nice but were obviously just beta software.

The main issue with this game as it stands is it is still that - beta. It's as if absolutely no QA was done to the game before release. No matter how much I dislike "early access" or beta title on Steam, I find it surprising Monomyth didn't go this route or at least run a short closed beta to get input from users on functionality and bugs.

As it stands the current version is pretty much just the beta with more content and more bugs. The game is riddled with tiny bugs and typos that would have been found by a normal group of testers. It's also riddled with usability issues.

[list]
[*] The lack of a clear tutorial is confusing - and piecing together how you're supposed to go about things using peepr is a PITA.
[*] The UI is stale and unintuitive. Very few of the buttons in the UI you need to press are actually animated - with no indication you've moused over them or that they are a button.
[*] Another UI issue - no skip buttons? No way to skip over cutscenes.
[*] Lack of customization - why even offer a screen to customize your character when you've got 3 combinations?
[/list]

Overall with those usability issues and the current bugs, I'm going to have to say I can't recommend this. Follow the project, see if they fix things up in a timely manner - but if you didn't already buy it years ago - you're probably better off waiting to see if you can get a better experience.

The UI is horrible. I find that the most difficult part of missions is fighting the UI to layout stuff the way I want it or to switch back and forth between profiles. The missions feel repetitive and just like I’m doing a bunch of busy work.  There are also a lot of bugs in the UI

It gives you the illusion of choice, but even if you say you don’t want to do something (such as like someone on the dating app, or add them to your codex) it does it anyway which is annoying.

A few things that would make the UI easier to use. 

1) Get rid of the map, or at least stop it from scrolling, I spend so much time trying to scroll the map back to where I the last suspect was. 
2) When using the codex at home let me dismiss profiles.  
3) Increase the detail of items in the strongbox, also let me put more stuff in it. 
4) Stop making me click a thousand times for each conversation. 
5) Get rid of the end cutscene after the mission where you talk about each individual, its not needed and just waste my time.

The game had a few, in my opinion minor, flaws at the start but it's still fun. I enjoy the fact that this game actually makes me think and look for little details. I was confused by the lack of tutorial but I managed to figure things out and I am glad to see they have since added one in. The devs are releasing daily fixes and seem to be staying on top of things and actually listening to feedback. 

TL;DR: Game was pretty good; Devs making constant improvents: now game is better.
